brief.instructions: Improve current cost-throughput frontier using deployment changes, not publication novelty. Generate at most two distinct hypotheses. First investigate safety-qualified activation of currently-profile-disabled DSpark adaptive verification, preserving draft k5 and graph-safe decode; require comparison against static k2/k5/no-spec within same topology, not claim topology comparison isolates k. Second only if justified investigate schedulable mixed-prefill verification cost calibration or graph-aware prefix allocation derived from DScale/EVICT, distinguishing already-existing upstream behavior. Treat source reports as claims, not reproduced facts. Strong negative evidence59970 and62541 must be addressed. Do not suggest blind batch-local dynamic k in DP because45963 disables it for collective divergence. Unknown deployed flags mandate cheap inspection before GPU execution.

card.statement: Inspect the deployed launch flags, checkout, patch, and container first: the supplied profile says DSpark k5 has adaptive verification disabled, while its CSV says DSpark is off. If verification is inactive and the DeepSeek-specific graph safety conditions are present or can be qualified, enable adaptive verification while retaining draft k5. The proposed mechanism is to spend less target verification work when a full drafted block is unlikely to be useful. This is a transfer inference, not an observed B200 benefit. The B300 concurrent-prefill failure makes mixed-batch graph eligibility a prerequisite, and the B200 tuning PR favors fixed k5. Advance only if same-topology tests improve SLO-qualified cost and throughput without sampling, rollback, or latency regressions.

policy.baseline_comparison: The supplied baseline reports a 2×DEP4 R7b profile with “DSpark k5 adaptive false,” while “CSV dspark_config off contradicts profile on; runtime flags not inspected.” Inspect deployed flags and freeze the checkout, patch, and container before attributing a delta. Compare adaptive verification with static k2, static k5, and no speculation within the same topology and fixed traces. The reported R7b and R10 results use different layouts and load points, so they do not isolate speculation.

criteria.description: Required veto: a credible, testable path to the specified cost and latency metrics, plus either a baseline delta or a cheap deployed-flag inspection that resolves whether the feature is already active. Unknown bottlenecks defer judgment.
criteria.justification: The baseline flags conflict. The requested 5% expected-gain threshold is an engineering target, not an observed effect. A flag inspection can establish whether an activation experiment has a meaningful baseline.

criteria.description: Required veto: preserve the exact sampling distribution, KV rollback, draft k5, and graph-safe decode; qualify concurrent-prefill safety before activation.
criteria.justification: The supplied issue title says “illegal memory access under concurrent prefill.” Its conditions and resolution are unknown from the title alone, so safety cannot be scored as established.

criteria.description: Specify same-topology static k2/k5/no-spec comparisons, fixed tokenizer and traces, both goodput scorers, latency tails, ITL length cohorts, and correctness. Isolate the adaptive toggle from any safety patch or calibrator.
criteria.justification: These controls address the supplied layout and scorer confounds without demanding a measured speedup before an experiment is proposed.

criteria.description: Inspect the relevant configuration and code paths, the reported negative evidence in 59970 and 62541, and existing upstream behavior before selecting a second hypothesis.
criteria.justification: The supplied items provide titles, not implementation details. Existing flags, ports, and parameter changes remain eligible; publication status has no selection penalty.

evidence.rationale: One relevant engineering source can establish a known implementation path; two sources or a paper are not automatic requirements. The supplied PR and issue titles are insufficient to establish code behavior or resolve failures, so affected judgments remain deferred. Hardware, workload, effect size, and limitations for the three listed fulltexts are unknown because their contents were not supplied.

policy.objective: Prioritize at most two testable deployment hypotheses for improving SLO-qualified goodput per GPU dollar and cost per successful million output tokens on the specified 8×B200 workload. Investigate safety-qualified DSpark adaptive verification first; consider verification-cost calibration or graph-aware prefix allocation only if the first investigation and upstream inspection justify it.
policy.rationale: Observed in the supplied baseline report, not reproduced here: R7b c512 is reported as 33.76 req/s with E2E p95 19.49 s; R10 DEP8 k2 c1024 is reported as 43.55 req/s with E2E p95 29.61 s. Author claims available here are limited to titles, including “Disable dynamic speculative decoding when DP is enabled” and the concurrent-prefill issue title; the negative details of 62541 are unknown. Transfer inference: adaptive verification could improve the target frontier only if deployed flags show a real inactive baseline, the safety conditions are resolved, and same-topology tests show SLO-qualified value. The 75-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not an estimated success probability. Failure of a required criterion vetoes selection; an unknown judgment defers it. No GPU result or gain is claimed, and transfer from B300, GLM, or A100 is unknown.

retrieval.rationale: This response uses only supplied material, as requested. The rubric calls for later repository and runtime inspection before selection or GPU execution; literature adds no necessary evidence at this stage.

assessment.meaning: Eligible for experiment design only; not scientifically validated or a measured improvement
reasons: correctness_and_safety: The design retains draft k5 and gates activation on sampling, KV rollback, and graph-safe mixed-prefill checks. Safety is unresolved: issue #59970 reports “IMA within 1 min at c96 (4/4)” on B300, while PR #59986 says its B300 reproducer was “Not run.” Neither establishes safety on the target B200 deployment.

causal_test.rationale: It compares adaptive k5 with static k5, static k2, and no speculation on the same topology and fixed traces, with both scorers, latency tails, ITL cohorts, and correctness checks. It isolates the adaptive toggle from a safety patch and calibrator. The proposed 5% threshold is a decision rule, not an observed gain.

correctness_and_safety.rationale: The design retains draft k5 and gates activation on sampling, KV rollback, and graph-safe mixed-prefill checks. Safety is unresolved: issue #59970 reports “IMA within 1 min at c96 (4/4)” on B300, while PR #59986 says its B300 reproducer was “Not run.” Neither establishes safety on the target B200 deployment.

implementation_evidence.rationale: The supplied pinned-code excerpt shows an adaptive graph-mode resolver, and the issue and PR bodies describe relevant paths. The effective launch flags, DeepSeek builder behavior, patch lineage, and container have not been inspected. PR #62541 reports that its qualified B200 lanes use “enable_adaptive_verification:false”; that is adverse deployment evidence, not a measured adaptive comparison.

task_value.rationale: The proposed read-only flag inspection can resolve whether adaptive verification is a deployment change: the supplied brief says “CSV dspark_config off contradicts profile on; runtime flags not inspected.” Same-topology comparisons make the cost and latency hypothesis testable. Target benefit and bottleneck remain unknown. The reported R7b and R10 results do not isolate speculation.

objections: Reported observation, not reproduced here: #59970 says throughput with adaptive verification disabled was “the same within noise” as adaptive verification with FULL_DECODE_ONLY on its B300 workload. The proposal should name this negative result explicitly.
Author claim: #62541 describes a qualified B200 full-k5 setting and reports a successful sweep, but supplies no same-topology adaptive-versus-static effect for this target.
Transfer inference: reducing verification work might improve 8×B200 SLO-qualified cost-throughput. Its sign and effect size are unknown; B300 safety results and GLM/B300 gains do not establish them.
review.required_revision: Explicitly carry forward #59970’s reported no-gain result and #62541’s fixed-k5 qualification as counterevidence. Inspect effective flags and freeze checkout, patch, and container; qualify mixed-prefill graph safety before any activation test.

decision_rules.inconclusive: CI spans the decision threshold; baseline cannot be pinned; scorer disagreement changes ranking; unstable load; bottleneck not observable; or budget exhausted.
decision_rules.reject: Correctness/safety violation; or confirmation CI upper bound excludes meaningful 5% benefit throughout target regimes; or >5% p95 guard regression. Distinguish mechanism failure from deployment inapplicability.
decision_rules.support: Design choice: at least 5% SLO-capacity goodput improvement over the strongest matched static control, with paired 95% CI lower bound above zero and all guards met. At fixed offered load, use at least 5% p95 latency reduction with noninferior goodput. These thresholds are proposed, not predicted gains.

sequential_budget.stop: Stop on correctness failure, baseline mismatch, sustained queue growth, or >10% tail regression. Preserve logs and scope.
